theory: A straight conductor of length $L$ carrying a current $I$ at right angles to a magnetic field $B$ feels a force
at right angles to both the current and the field; its direction is given by Fleming's left-hand rule and reverses when the current is reversed.

Here the conductor is held rigidly and the magnets sit on a top-pan balance. By Newton's third law the magnets feel an equal and opposite force, so the balance reading changes by $\Delta m = F/g$, and $F = (m - m_0)g$.
A graph of $F$ against $I$ is a straight line through the origin with slope $BL$, so $B = \text{slope}/L$.

apparatus.magnets: Two flat magnets on a U-shaped steel yoke (opposite poles facing).
apparatus.rod: Stiff copper rod held by clamp stands through the gap, not touching the magnets.
apparatus.supply: DC power supply, rheostat and ammeter, with a reversing switch.
apparatus.ruler: Ruler to measure the width of the poles (the length of rod in the field).

safety: The rod gets warm at high currents: keep currents below 5 A and switch off between readings.
Keep the strong magnets away from phones, cards and the balance's electronics.
steps: With no current, record the balance reading m₀ (or tare the balance to zero).
Measure the width of the poles L with a ruler.
Switch on and set a current I with the rheostat; read the ammeter and the balance m.
Repeat for at least six currents, all in the same direction.
Reverse the current and note what happens to the reading (Fleming's left-hand rule).
Work out F = (m − m₀)g and plot F against I.
tips: Make sure the rod does not touch the magnets or the yoke.
Tare or read m₀ with the current OFF.
Keep all your readings with the current in one direction, or treat the reversed ones separately.
references: Young, H. D. & Freedman, R. A. University Physics, ch. 27: Magnetic field and magnetic forces.
Physics Bench virtual laboratory — current balance practical.

noZeroReading.title: Record the balance reading with no current, m₀
noZeroReading.detail: The force comes from the change in reading: F = (m − m₀)g. Without m₀ (or a tared balance, m₀ = 0) the forces cannot be worked out.

mixedDirections.title: Some readings are below m₀
mixedDirections.detail: Those were taken with the current reversed, so the force on the magnets was the other way. Keep one direction for your graph, and describe the reversal in your discussion.

massNotForce.title: F is a force in newtons, not a mass
massNotForce.detail: Multiply the change in mass (in kg) by g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹: a change of 1.20 g gives F = 0.00120 × 9.81 = 0.0118 N = 11.8 mN.

neverReversed.title: Try reversing the current
neverReversed.detail: This practical also demonstrates the direction of the force. Reverse the current and explain the change in reading with Fleming's left-hand rule.

taredWithCurrent.title: The balance was tared with the current on
taredWithCurrent.detail: Taring then hides the force you want to measure. Switch off, tare, then switch on again.
